Method: each `test-<module>-*` file run via `parity/preload.mjs` with
`PARITY_TARGET=<module>` (30s timeout per file). Pass rates are **raw** —
they do not subtract `parity/expected-failures.shim.json` entries.

> Note (2026-10-14): `parity/run.mjs` now uses exact module matching
> (`test-<mod>.js` or `test-<mod>-*.js`). Previously `startsWith("test-http")`
> also caught `test-http2-*`/`test-https-*` (743 files instead of 399 for http).

Re-baseline (2026-11-22): the recorded v24 total (2,324/3,206) was re-measured on current main 7f4610fe with the current harness (evidence: `shim-before-after/main/` — 41 CSVs + SUMMARY.md + `logs/adjudication.log` in the parity-sweep goal workspace; audit report `shim-before-after-audit.md`). Raw sweep 2,265/3,206 (−59); after isolated 2x adjudication, 8 sweep-only flakes pass, so the genuine net is **−51 (64 regressions − 13 flips)**: recorded 2,324/3,206 → **2,273/3,206 (70.9%)**. Concentrated in stream −26 (iter port + Brotli gap), crypto −11 and fs −11 (sweep −12/−13 before the 3 flakes); counter-flips events +8 (recorded 1/9 was stale), http2 +3, http +2 (net 0 after its 2 regressions). Per-module counts below are the adjudicated numbers. CI’s parity job covers only `path punycode querystring string_decoder events assert`, which is why the drift went uncaught.

## Take-back wave (2026-11-23)

Six lanes (PRs #551–#556) took back the good parts of the old Gen 0 shims into current main. Net v24: **+32 (2,273/3,206 → 2,305/3,206)**. Node26 unchanged at **2,374/2,814**.

- L-Z (PR #551): zlib API change only — `Z_*` constants as non-enumerable CJS properties on the default export. 0 flips (v24 52/65, node26 69/89 unchanged).
- L-C (PR #552): child_process 6/112 → **7/112** (+1, 0 regressions) — execSync validates null-byte args before getShell().
- L-HARNESS (PR #553): timer-restore harness for the cluster/dgram sweep path — cluster 4/83 → **22/83** (+18), dgram 1/80 → **14/80** (+13), inspector 38/75 unchanged, 0 src/ changes.
- L-H (PR #554) then REVERTED (PR #555): the standalone-response trailing-empty-write flip (v24 http 388 → 389) was reverted — Node 26's test expects 1 write, the v24 file expects 2, and one fixed count cannot satisfy both, so Node 26 wins. Net 0: v24 http 388/397, node26 http 412/422 unchanged. The MIT license line from #554 stays in src/http.js.
- L-SW (PR #556): capability restoration — `Server._handleFetch` (Service Worker / Fetch-API server transport) as an opt-in adapter over `handleRequest`. 0 flips, http counts unchanged.

## Not swept

- **http** (399 test files, exact match): Hang diagnosed 2026-10-14. NOT a single
  deadlock — it's death by a thousand timeouts. ~30% of http tests (abort,
  destroyed-socket, keep-alive, agent lifecycle) hang the full 30s spawn timeout
  because the shim leaks socket handles in abort/destroy scenarios (event loop
  never drains). 399 files × 30% × 30s ≈ 60 min. Root cause: product bug in
  src/http.js / src/net.js socket lifecycle, not harness. Also fixed: run.mjs
  was matching 743 files (http+http2+https) via startsWith — now exact.
- **constants, punycode, sys**: zero official test files — "no official tests".
- Internal shims with no test target (`_http_*`, `_stream_*`, `_tls_*`, `node_globals`, `fetch-patch`, `browser-builds`, etc.): not applicable.

## Notes for prioritization

- **events 9/9 (re-baseline 2026-11-22)**: the recorded 1/9 was stale since Oct 11 — all 9 pass isolated 2x. The old “misleading” note no longer applies.
- **buffer 60/62**: the 2 failures are the documented expected failures — effectively at parity.
- **Fixable-first candidates** (real gaps, browser-achievable): `fs`, `stream`, `async_hooks`, `dns`, `zlib`, `vm`, `tls`, `http2`.
- **Inherent / deprioritize**: `dgram` (no UDP in browser), `child_process`/`cluster` (no real processes), `domain` (deprecated), `sea` (likely N/A).
- `sqlite` should go the WASM-of-the-real-thing route (wa-sqlite), not hand-rolled.

## Node 26 re-target (26-suite, Node 26.13.1 tests vs the shims)

Separate program from the v24 ranking above: different test suite (Node 26.13.1 `test/parallel` files, staged into `parity/node-test/` and run via `parity/drift/run-baseline.mjs`), different totals — the two tables are not comparable.

Baseline (`parity/drift/node26-baseline.jsonc`, 2026-11-19): 2,748 run — 2,144 pass / 575 fail / 29 timeout. Oracle (`parity/drift/node26-oracle.json`): 563 true shim-gap / 27 fails-natively / 5 native-timeout (triage corrected 9 oracle entries; see `NOTES-26-triage-index.md`). Ceiling ~2,297/2,748 (83.6%).

Wave 1 (PRs #507–#521, 15 lanes, 2026-11-19/20): 53 net flips — 2,144 → 2,197/2,748 (80.0%). Wave 2 (PRs #522–#529, 8 lanes, 2026-11-20): 75 flips — 2,197 → 2,272/2,748 (82.7%). Wave 3 (PRs #531–#534, 4 lanes, 2026-11-20): 51 flips — 2,272 → 2,323/2,748 (84.5%), above the triage ceiling of ~2,297: repl highlight repair (PR #531, +1), http2 WR/W1/C1 (PR #532, +6), zlib Zip API (PR #533, +15), stream iter port (PR #534, +29 net — 33 flips minus 4 brotli NO-FIX regressions, documented in NOTES-26-stream-l6.md). All counts parent-verified on live main (suite re-runs + isolated adjudication); per-lane evidence in `NOTES-26-*.md`.

Wave 4 (PR #537, 2026-11-21): folded the 65 unrun in-scope tests into the program record (triage in `NOTES-26-unrun-triage.md`, per-group evidence in `NOTES-26-unrun-*.md`): 39 already pass under the harness (33 true shim passes + 6 that never touch the shim), 8 flippable — all events, flipped by the E-26-W4 lane — and 18 NO-FIX (all http2 diagnostics-channel). Program 2,323/2,748 → 2,370/2,813 (84.3%). The headline moves from 84.5% to 84.3% because the 18 http2 NO-FIX tests enter the denominator with 0 passes — a measurement artifact of folding in the unrun tests, not a regression. Events reaches 39/39 (100%).

Re-sweep (2026-11-22): full-program re-measurement on main with the fixed drift tool (`parity/drift/run-baseline.mjs` now honors each test's `// Flags:` header). All 28 modules re-swept, every diff adjudicated isolated 2x (evidence in `NOTES-26-resweep-flags.md`): **2,370/2,813 → 2,372/2,813 (84.3%)**, 0 regressions. Two measurement corrections, no code change: `test-process-redirect-warnings.js` (process 88 → 89/102; the triage had classified it "not a gap, sweep race") and `test-readline-promises-csi.mjs` (readline 21 → 22/22; passes under its `// Flags: --expose-internals` header, now honored — the flag-caused flip the re-sweep was designed to find). The one uncounted file the re-sweep surfaced, `test-eventemitter-asyncresource.js`, stays uncounted: it passes natively (Node 26.13.1, exit 0) but fails under the shim (exit 1, 2x — `EventEmitterAsyncResource` requires `options.name` where Node defaults it), a real shim gap and a candidate fix lane, not a fold-in.

Fold-in (2026-11-22): the asyncresource lane fixed `test-eventemitter-asyncresource.js` (name defaults to the subclass name, per Node 26), so the test is folded into the program record — events 39/39 → **40/40**, program **2,372/2,813 → 2,373/2,814 (84.3%)**. The headline percentage does not move.

Flip (2026-11-22): the http2 engine design study's every-5th sample of the failing set found `test-http2-write-callbacks.js` passing on current main — it was failing at the Nov 18 wave end and was never banked. Re-verified isolated 2x on main `f89551e7` (oracle exit 0 2x, shim exit 0 2x, empty output). No code change: http2 94/307 → **95/307 (30.9%)**, program **2,373/2,814 → 2,374/2,814 (84.4%)**. The headline percentage moves 84.3% → 84.4%.

Correction: repl Wave 1 is 97/108, not 98 — the util merge (#513) regressed `test-repl-highlight.js` (proven by one-step bisection against the pre-util merge); the repair is a Wave 3 follow-up. Wave 2 took repl 97 → 99/108. Wave 3 repaired it to 100/108 (PR #531).
